A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MimiCAT/PokeAnimDB research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original pose-transfer comparisons in Table 2, component ablations in Section 5, and qualitative results throughout the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a perceptual user study in Appendix A4.4 and Table A2.

M1.justification: The correspondence and pose-transfer transformers, quaternion initialization, pose prior, training objectives and ARAP refinement remain unchanged. Appendix A2 retains the same pose-prior architecture and objectives.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Mixamo, AMASS and PokeAnimDB, humanoid and cross-category transfer evaluations, and text-to-motion applications. The added user study changes assessment of pose-transfer quality without documenting a new character domain, dataset or transfer task.

E2.justification: NPT, CGT, SFPT and TapMo remain the comparison methods. The new user study uses this same set, while the hierarchical-correspondence comparison and ablation are retained. AnyTop is newly cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix A4.4 adds a protocol involving 50 Prolific participants assessing 20 transfer pairs using 1–5 ratings for pose similarity and geometric quality, plus best-method choices. Existing splits, training budgets, PMD/ELS metrics and benchmark sample counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new user study examines whether human judgments corroborate the quantitative comparison, adding perceptual validation. The three component ablations and existing cycle-consistency case studies are unchanged; Figure 9's added highlights redisplay existing evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the empirical comparisons. The user study adds point averages and a preference percentage without uncertainty analysis; participant counts describe its evaluation sample.

E6.justification: Table 2's benchmark and ablation values are unchanged. New Table A2 reports MimiCAT ratings of 4.076 for pose similarity and 4.102 for geometric quality, versus the strongest baseline ratings of 3.364 (SFPT) and 3.605 (TapMo), respectively. Appendix A4.4 also reports 60.0% best-method votes.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and A1–A3 retain the same mathematical content, including quaternion averaging and the matrix-Fisher formulation. Equation compaction changes typography, without adding or revising assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: category-free transfer, PokeAnimDB, the soft-correspondence cascade transformer and superior transfer with downstream applications. Limited wording changes do not alter the scientific scope of these claims.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and Appendix A5's limitations remain unchanged, including predicted-rigging errors, attention costs and missing temporal consistency. The user-study discussion corroborates the existing quality-ranking interpretation without introducing a new mechanism or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: v2 removes the introduction's explicit promise to make code and data publicly available for research. Implementation, hyperparameter, hardware and preprocessing disclosures remain unchanged. This deletion changes release information but does not establish that actual resource availability changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds AnyTop: Character Animation Diffusion with Any Topology as reference 19 in the correspondence-learning discussion. Other references match across renumbering and bibliographic updates; research positioning is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: v2 lightly edits the abstract and introduction, removes the author email line, standardizes bibliography text and adds the user-study subsection. It also corrects the displayed project address to match the hyperlink destination already present in v1. The overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table A2 and red highlight boxes within Figure 9's existing closeups. Table 1, Figure 6 and Table A1 move between columns, and equation/table spacing is tightened. Existing qualitative examples are retained.

improvement.justification: The added 50-participant, 20-pair study supplies direct human assessment beyond v1's automatic metrics and illustrative examples, modestly strengthening evidence of perceptual transfer quality. Limited coverage and absent uncertainty reporting constrain this gain. Removing the code/data-release promise reduces clarity about future access, but the added empirical support provides a modest net improvement.
